planNotes.claim: The plan price comes back as machine time and does not roll over.
planNotes.quote: A plan sets how many sandboxes can run at once and how fast you can start them. It includes a month of machine time equal to its price; included time does not roll over.

planNotes.claim: Organization plans are per seat; concurrency and start limits multiply by seats, storage does not.
planNotes.quote: An organization plan is **per seat**: the plan price × seats.

planNotes.claim: Organization storage is one amount from the plan, not multiplied by seats.
planNotes.quote: An organization has one amount, from its plan (not multiplied by seats).

compute.cpuBasisNote: One flat price per size for as long as the sandbox runs. vCPUs are shared; RAM is reserved for the sandbox.
compute.cpuBasisQuote: vCPUs are shared; RAM is reserved for the sandbox.
compute.billingIncrementNote: Metered per second, from up until stopped. A large sandbox for ten minutes uses 1,200 default-seconds.
compute.minimumNote: not published: no minimum seconds or minimum charge is stated anywhere on the pricing or billing pages.
compute.ratesSameOnEveryPlanQuote: One dollar buys 100,000 of them, so a `large` sandbox running ten minutes uses 1,200 seconds.
compute.quote: Metering is per second, from the moment a sandbox is up until it is stopped.

sizeNotes.quote: `xlarge` needs the $100/month plan or higher. Lower plans get `403 machine_class_plan_required`.

sizeNotes.claim: Disk is on top of the OS image.
sizeNotes.quote: "Disk" is space for your files, added on top of the OS image; the OS and pre-installed tools don't count against it.

storage.diskIncluded: 50 GB on the $20 plan, 250 GB on $100, 1 TB on $500, 5 TB on $2,000; 10 GB on the trial or with no plan; 50 GB with time packs and no plan. Counts stopped sandboxes (disk, memory and automatic snapshots) and named snapshots; running sandboxes do not count.
storage.diskIncludedQuote: Storage isn't billed: each plan includes an amount for what you keep, **sandboxes that aren't running** (stopped or failed: their disk, memory and automatic snapshots) and **named snapshots**.
storage.billedWhileStoppedNote: Stopped sandboxes cost nothing; their disk and snapshots count only toward the included storage quota.
storage.stoppedRetentionNote: No expiry published: kept until you delete the sandbox.
storage.quote: Nothing. Its disk, memory snapshot and automatic snapshots are kept at no charge until you delete it; they count toward your plan's included storage (50 GB on the $20 plan).

snapshots.note: Named snapshots have no separate charge; automatic snapshots are free. Both count toward the included storage.
snapshots.quote: They have no separate charge. Keep as many as you like; they count toward your plan's included storage.

overage.behaviour: New sandboxes, forks and named-snapshot saves are refused with 402 storage_limit_reached until you free space or upgrade; optional auto-delete can remove least-recently-used stopped sandboxes after an email notice.
overage.quote: At or over it, new sandboxes (including from templates and share codes), forks and named-snapshot saves answer `402 storage_limit_reached` until you delete stopped sandboxes or named snapshots, or upgrade.

storage.quotasQuote: **Storage included:** 50 GB on the $20 plan, 250 GB on the $100 plan, 1 TB on the $500 plan, 5 TB on the $2,000 plan; 10 GB on the trial or without a plan.

other.note: One-off, same per-size rates, never expire; plan time is spent first.
other.quote: **Time packs:** $20 each at the same rates; they never expire.
An organization plan is **per seat**: the plan price × seats.

other.note: No public IPv4 of its own: private IPv4 behind NAT plus a public IPv6 address per sandbox. No price because it is not offered.
other.quote: Private IPv4 (NAT) and a **public IPv6** address per sandbox

other.note: Not offered; only a rename of the sandbox's own subdomain, or a CNAME you terminate yourself.
other.quote: Point a CNAME at the hosted hostname and terminate TLS yourself (for example with a proxy in front), or run Caddy inside the sandbox on its IPv6 address (after `sudo ufw allow 80,443/tcp`). First-class custom domains are on the roadmap.

other.priceUsd: the plan price; every dollar returns as machine time
other.quote: The plan fee is not a fee on top: every dollar comes back as machine time.

trial.quote: During the trial, TTLs above eight hours and `--no-auto-stop` are refused.

hermes.summary: Sandboxer documents no Hermes recipe and does not preinstall the Hermes CLI. The route is a sandbox with no auto-stop, then the vendor's own installer over SSH, then a systemd service for the gateway.
steps: hermes setup / hermes model, then hermes gateway
Enable a systemd unit with Restart=always so the gateway survives a cold boot
sbx host <port> if the Hermes web dashboard must be reachable

quotes.quote: For anything that must survive cold boots and forks, make it a systemd service:

hermes.note: The preinstalled-agent list does not include Hermes or OpenClaw, and Sandboxer's prompt API accepts only claude-code, codex, opencode, pi, prime-agent, kimi and mistral.

openclaw.summary: Same as Hermes: nothing preinstalled, no guide. Install OpenClaw in a sandbox and run its gateway under systemd; expose the port with sbx host.

quotes.quote: Install OpenClaw, run onboarding, and chat with your AI assistant in about 5 minutes.

dashboardOnly.answer: Partly, and better than the other two on this point: the dashboard shows each sandbox with a countdown and an Extend button, an Open desktop button, a Terminal tab and a Billing page, and the hosted MCP server lets Claude or ChatGPT create and drive sandboxes after an OAuth sign-in, with no terminal. But no template gallery or one-click agent exists, so installing Hermes or OpenClaw still needs a shell.
dashboardOnly.quote: Apps like Claude and ChatGPT sign in with your Sandboxer account (OAuth).

supportingQuote.quote: The dashboard shows a countdown ("Stops in") on every sandbox with an **Extend** button.
